answer: Clones share a brain, and brains leave fingerprints where they fail. Auditors can slip each seat a few high-entropy riddles, prompts where independent models scatter widely, the way a plume of smoke splits in gusty wind. Honest agents disagree with one another; copies of one model and prompt give the same odd answer. Seats matching on more than 9 of 12 such probes (assumed threshold) get pooled into one paid seat. Like a falcon watching for birds that flinch in unison, the auditor's signal is shared error, not shared truth.
